feature: Generalized read-consent flow for Buy.tsx purchase sessions (Git #1311, Epic #1309 Phase 2): session-keyed read-consent URL mint with server-resolved requirement (required vs optional), the explicit Retainer skip branch, its fail-closed refusal for Monitoring, and the skip's visibility on consent-status.
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the #1311 backend extraction only — no UI is wired to these routes yet (Buy.tsx wiring is Phase 8, #1309). Every call is either the genuine PUBLIC intake (POST /api/public/checkout-session, minting a real checkout_sessions row + funnel lead per run — same accepted side effect as billing/retainer-signup.json's CREATE) or a session-keyed public flow route.

PRODUCT SLUGS are real catalog rows confirmed against the live services table: architect-essentials-retainer (serviceType 'retainer' — the ONLY serviceType whose read consent is optional/skippable) and monitoring-foundation-smb (serviceType 'monitoring_tier' — consent required, skip must be refused 409).

WHAT CANNOT BE ASSERTED HERE, honestly: the Microsoft admin-consent screen itself and GET /api/consent/callback's grant stamping — the OAuth wall is architecturally undrivable by this harness (same caveat as copilot-readiness/money-path-e2e.json). The callback's skip-clearing branch (consentSkippedAt back to null when a real grant lands) is covered by unit tests in artifacts/api-server/src/routes/consent.test.ts instead.
The two sessions minted per run expire in 24h and are never consented/paid — no account, tenant, or grant is ever created by this manifest.

apiTests.name: CREATE (retainer) — mint a purchase session for a Retainer product; extract sessionId
URL (retainer) — GET /api/public/flow/read-consent-url resolves the requirement server-side from the catalog: a Retainer session is optional
URL (retainer) — skippable flag is true for the optional product
URL (retainer) — the minted URL is the session-state Microsoft admin-consent URL (state = the session UUID, /common/adminconsent)
SKIP (retainer) — POST /api/public/flow/read-consent-skip records the explicit skip on the session row (the real backend branch behind Buy.tsx's 'Skip — buy without a scan')
STATUS (retainer) — the recorded skip is visible to the flow: GET /api/public/flow/consent-status reports readConsentSkipped true
CREATE (monitoring) — mint a purchase session for a Monitoring tier; extract sessionId
URL (monitoring) — the same route reports required (not skippable) for a Monitoring session
SKIP REFUSED (monitoring) — the skip is a privileged branch: a required product's session is refused 409 consent_required, server-side, regardless of what the caller asks
STATUS (monitoring) — no skip was recorded for the refused session
SESSION GUARD — an unknown session UUID is refused by the same resolveFlowSession contract as every sibling flow route (404 session_expired)
